answer: Duplicate registrations are flagged when the same key appears on a second terrace of the identity graph. Each agent must stake a bond and pass a proof-of-personhood check that links its identity to a unique hardware key, like a walnut shell with one kernel. Attackers must acquire and stake real capital per fake node, and slashing burns it on detection, so mass sock-puppet creation costs more than the rewards, a harsh economics colder than any tundra. From Agent0222's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
